what: Spatial overlays, including flood, riparian and wetlands, are tested against the address point with ST_Contains rather than the lot polygon.
why: A lot partly intersecting a land-based overlay can be shown as outside it, and its applicable rules can then be omitted. The nearby Greenweb code explicitly recognises that partial lot overlap is binding.
fix: Resolve the cadastral lot geometry and use ST_Intersects for land-based overlays; if geometry is unavailable, mark the overlay check not checked. Add a route test where the address point is outside an overlay but the lot intersects it.

what: Missing overlay results render as "No"; the same pattern affects flood, acid sulfate, landslide, biodiversity, additional uses, foreshore, reservation, riparian and wetlands.
why: An absent value can mean an unchecked or failed lookup, but this live assessment tab tells the user the constraint does not apply. The component already has a notChecked helper for other tiles, showing the intended three-state model.
fix: Use the existing notChecked state for every overlay tile before rendering "No", and add component tests for absent and failed overlay data.

what: A failed or non-OK structured-SEPP request leaves the result arrays empty, after which the UI says "No Housing SEPP structured requirements".
why: The SEPP tab is part of the live property assessment. A timeout, rejected request, or HTTP error is indistinguishable from a successful empty result and suppresses the required not-checked disclosure.
fix: Track a structured-SEPP load error separately; render "State requirements not checked" unless an empty response was successfully received. Add tests for rejected and non-OK fetches.

what: Hardcoded zone lists and planning thresholds determine Housing SEPP, CDC, TOD and ADG applicability.
why: These literals are consumed by the assessment's StateLevelControls eligibility filtering, so a planning amendment can cause rules to be included or excluded for the wrong property. Project rules explicitly prohibit hardcoded zone uses and standards.
fix: Replace each eligibility decision used by the assessment with the existing property-specific Planning Portal or extracted-provision data, returning not checked when unavailable; add fixtures covering an amended or uncovered zone.
intentional: intentional: comments explicitly centralise and document the literals, but they are not sourced from the database or an official API.

what: The generated production granny-flat PDF prints a hardcoded Schedule 1 table containing floor areas, setbacks, height, open-space and landscape figures.
why: The report presents these as applicable CDC requirements, but the values are neither loaded from extracted provisions nor tied to an effective-date source. They can silently become stale or use the wrong lot-size band.
fix: Pass the applicable, sourced provision rows into the report and render their text and citation; show not checked when a row is unavailable. Add a report fixture proving the displayed values come from source data.
intentional: intentional: the comment identifies the intended Schedule 1 source, but the implementation reconstructs and embeds its figures.

what: canSubdivide uses a fixed 450 m² minimum to remove subdivision requirements.
why: The threshold is not property- or council-specific. Consumers use its false result to hide requirements, so an Inner West assumption can omit applicable rules for another planning instrument or an amended control.
fix: Require a sourced minimum-lot value at the call site and do not suppress subdivision requirements when it is unavailable. Add tests for unavailable data and differing sourced minima.
intentional: intentional: the comment describes this as a conservative Inner West threshold, but it is still a typed regulatory figure.

what: The live Pattern Book eligibility card states hardcoded 300 m² and 1500 m² minimum lot sizes.
why: This is served directly in the State assessment tab as an explanation of CDC eligibility. It can become inaccurate independently of the API-derived numeric eligibility result beside it.
fix: Derive the displayed range from the sourced eligibility details, or omit the range when no sourced values are available. Add a rendered-card test using changed source values.

what: A local APARTMENT_RESTRICTED_ZONES list decides whether to warn that the property's zone may prohibit apartment development.
why: Zone permissibility is council- and LEP-specific. This manual list can give a wrong property-specific warning instead of using the applicable LEP permissibility result.
fix: Use the property's sourced LEP permissibility response for the warning, and show not checked when it is unavailable. Add tests for a zone whose permissibility differs by council.
intentional: intentional: comments document a deliberate manual taxonomy update, but it remains an unsourced regulatory zone list.
